title: Experimental procedure of household activities and physical activity
author: Unknown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jauciew

steps.title: Explain and practice SCWT
steps.instruction: Explain the Stroop Color‑Word Test (SCWT) to participants and have them practice 10 sheets (six congruent, four incongruent) on the screen, answering each word and advancing with the Enter key.

steps.title: Set up cortical fNIRS optodes
steps.instruction: Cover the participants’ frontal area with 27 optodes (14 light emitters, 13 detectors) anchored at Fpz (10‑20 system) to obtain 42‑channel cortical hemodynamic measurements; set detector‑emitter pair distance to 3.0 cm.

steps.title: Configure skin‑blood‑flow optodes
steps.instruction: Place three additional detector‑only optodes to the right, middle, and left of the prefrontal cortex for three‑channel skin blood‑flow measurement; set inter‑detector distance to 1.5 cm.

steps.title: Conduct SCWT block design
steps.instruction: Have participants sit with chin on the holder and perform the SCWT for a total of 5 min 30 s. Use a periodic block design: 30‑s task block followed by 20‑s rest block. Include three congruent and three incongruent task blocks (contents randomized) and seven rest blocks. Counterbalance whether the first block is congruent or incongruent using a random number table. Participants answer each word and press Enter to advance.

steps.title: Record sitting heart rate
steps.instruction: Measure each subject’s heart rate while they remain seated.

steps.title: Perform HA vacuuming experiment
steps.instruction: On a 2.2 × 1.8 m floor area scatter 8 g of paper shreds and 100 plastic balls (6 mm diameter). Instruct participants to vacuum the floor as completely as possible for 10 min, including retrieving the vacuum cleaner, plugging in the cord, vacuuming, unplugging, and returning the cleaner.

steps.title: Perform control vacuuming motion
steps.instruction: On the same 2.2 × 1.8 m floor area with no debris, have participants imitate the vacuuming motion for 10 min, retrieving only the vacuum cleaner at the start and returning it at the end.

steps.title: Record heart rate during tasks
steps.instruction: Record each participant’s heart rate every 2 min throughout both the HA vacuuming and control motion tasks.

steps.title: Provide seated rest period
steps.instruction: After each 10‑min task (HA or control), allow participants to sit quietly for a 5‑min rest.

steps.title: Repeat SCWT before each task
steps.instruction: Immediately before the HA vacuuming and before the control motion tasks, conduct the SCWT again using the same block design and procedure described earlier.

steps.title: Collect accomplishment rating
steps.instruction: After completing the HA experiment, ask participants to rate their feeling of accomplishment on a 5‑point Likert scale.

steps.title: Localize channel coordinates
steps.instruction: Use a 3D digitizer (FASTRAK, Polhemus, Colchester, VT, USA) and probabilistic registration to map channel coordinates onto the MNI template. Define six ROIs: right frontopolar (channels 21, 29, 38), left frontopolar (22, 31, 39), right dorsolateral (2, 3, 11, 12), left dorsolateral (6, 7, 14, 15), right ventrolateral (18, 35, 36), left ventrolateral (25, 41, 42).

steps.title: Process oxy‑Hb signals
steps.instruction: Convert oxy‑Hb signals to numerical values. Set baseline using the 0‑ to 5.0‑s interval of the rest period. Remove skin blood flow via segment‑independent component analysis (ICA) separating 42 cerebral channels and 3 skin channels; select the skin component with spatial uniformity coefficient > 0.5 and high correlation, then remove it. Apply a moving‑average filter to smooth the remaining oxy‑Hb data and suppress heart‑rate and respiration noise.

steps.title: Record supine heart rate
steps.instruction: On a separate day, have participants lie supine, rest for 15 min, then measure heart rate for 1 min while they remain silent and minimize movement.
